title: Did you know scope creep kills more projects than bad code ever will? 🤯
transcript: build it slow. Now, what I want you to understand at this point is that there's something called an MVP or a minimum viable product. One of the major issues with building a software product is something called scope creep. You start building something, then you just add to it and add to it and add to it and add to it until eventually you have this monstrous application, so many different features, and all these random things that introduce bugs and issues and problems that you never needed in the first place. This is why we started at the very beginning of the project by understanding what it is we actually wanted to build, what problem it was solving, and what done actually means. Generally speaking, when you build any type of software application, you want to build the minimum viable product first. That means you want to build the absolute minimum amount of features that allow this product to be usable. All great software companies have started this way, and this is exactly what you should aim to do, especially when you're building with AI.
